items.title: Coping with Being the One-Person UX Team
items.summary: How to maximize your impact when you are the sole UX specialist on your project or in your organization.

items.title: In Defense of Post-its
items.summary: Sticky notes strengthen team dynamics and represent an egalitarian, concise means for expressing ideas in UX design projects.

items.title: UX Expert Reviews
items.summary: Expert reviews involve the analysis of a design by a UX expert with the goal of identifying usability problems and strengths.

items.title: The 5 Steps to Service Blueprinting
items.summary: Five key steps comprise a framework for service blueprinting that can be scaled to any scope or timeline.

items.title: Why Personas Fail
items.summary: Personas are useful tools for UX work, so why do they often fail? Find out what pitfalls cause personas to fail, and how to avoid and overcome them.

items.title: Empathy Mapping: The First Step in Design Thinking
items.summary: Empathy maps help UX teams visualize user attitudes and behaviors, building a shared understanding of end users while highlighting gaps in existing user data.

items.title: Decision Frames: How Cognitive Biases Affect UX Practitioners
items.summary: Designers are vulnerable to the same cognitive biases as users. The context in which you present a problem can bias your design choices.

items.title: How to Deal With Bad Design Suggestions
items.summary: Gracefully respond to unsolicited design ideas, and prevent them from derailing good design. Turn them into UX learning experiences.

items.title: UX Mapping Methods Compared: A Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Empathy maps, customer journey maps, experience maps, and service blueprints depict different processes and have different goals, yet they all build common ground within an organization.

items.title: Ideation in Practice: How Effective UX Teams Generate Ideas
items.summary: Data from 257 UX professionals shows that quality UX ideas come from ideating early in the design cycle, drawing inspiration from user research, and working with a group. Many struggle with generating ideas because they lack time, managerial support, and a methodology for conducting effective ideation sessions.

items.title: 5 Strategies for Presenting UX Remotely
items.summary: Master remote presentations by creating the right environment, being human, reducing distractions, taking control, and telling a story.

items.title: Scaling Design Thinking to Fit Your Needs (and Budget)
items.summary: Design-thinking methods are flexible and scalable. You can apply them to a variety of design challenges regardless of budget and team size.

items.title: Bringing Personas to Agile
items.summary: Kim discusses ways to fit personas in Agile environments.

items.title: Service Blueprints: Definition
items.summary: Service blueprints visualize organizational processes in order to optimize how a business delivers a user experience.

items.title: Troubleshooting Group Ideation: 10 Fixes for More and Better UX Ideas
items.summary: Groups can bias individuals and impact collaborative ideation. A focus on getting as many ideas as possible can mitigate some of the negative group effects.

items.title: Personas vs. Jobs-to-Be-Done
items.summary: Jobs-to-be-done focus on user problems and needs, while well-executed personas include the same information and also add behavioral and attitudinal details.

items.title: Does Agile Destroy UX?
items.summary: As Agile UX evolves, so does the role of the UX practitioner. In modern software-development environments, UX helps define how products are developed.

items.title: Building Strong Designer-Developer Relationships
items.summary: Sarah Gibbons discusses techniques for fostering collaboration and communication among product team members.

items.title: Facilitating an Effective Design Studio Workshop
items.summary: Design studios are UX workshops that combine ideation and design critique with idea prioritization and help teams collaborate and feel invested in the project.

items.title: How to Prioritize Ideas from UX Brainstorming Sessions
items.summary: Use ranking techniques to help turn workshop ideas into concrete action plans.
